value.produces: aix433-full.qcow2 (AIX 4.3.3 + X11/CDE + Ultimedia Services + Netscape 4.08 + Quake 1.07, native on the emulated GXT130P) + golden; builds its own qemu-system-ppc into /opt/qemu-ppc-s3 first

labctl.notes: Framebuffer console only: AIX's LFT draws through the emulated Matrox GXT130P, and the pointer is PS/2 relative (no tablet on a 40p), so the daemon reckons absolute coordinates itself. No exec channel. Reset restores the in-qcow2 'golden' snapshot, which skips the genuine IBM firmware's POST entirely -- a cold boot walks that POST and takes 15-25 minutes.

render.stationsManifestPrelude:
# aix432 (slot 171) — IBM AIX 4.3.3 / CDE on an emulated RS/6000 7020 (40p):
#   qemu-system-ppc from the kernel-hive QEMU fork branch aix432-s3, installed
#   to /opt/qemu-ppc-s3 (pve-qemu ships no ppc target that can do this). TCG
#   only. The display is a Matrox MGA model written FOR this station and
#   claimed by AIX as the IBM GXT130P (mg21); the machine boots the GENUINE
#   IBM 40p boot ROM, whose PReP residual data is what brings up gxme0/rcm0/
#   lft0/paud0 at all. CDE renders natively at 1024x768x8 — no remote X.
#   NOT YET REGISTERED HERE: the entry is a candidate, so no emit stanza is
#   generated from it. Promotion needs the golden and a relay-reachable port.

deviceSetSummary: -M 40p,audiodev=snd0 -accel tcg -m 192 (the machine reports 128 MiB whatever is passed; -m 512 is refused outright)
-bios $ROMS/rs6k40p.BIN (the GENUINE IBM 7020-40P boot ROM; PREP_TB_FREQ=15000000 in the environment, and the POST settimeofday call must be skipped)
-vga mga (the Matrox MGA model added on this branch; AIX claims it as the GXT130P, mg21)
-drive file=$D/aix433-golden.qcow2,format=qcow2,if=scsi,bus=0,unit=0 (LSI 53c810 at PCI_DEVFN(1,0) — the machine has NO IDE)
-global cs4231a.dma=6 (AIX's CS4231 driver fixes play DMA at 6; QEMU defaults to 3. iobase 0x830 / IRQ 10 already match)

launcherParity.reason: the tracked launcher IS the deployed launcher (box-sync mirror pairs carry its rn-tapnet.sh and skipfix.py helpers); the golden was baked 2026-08-26 with this exact device set against binary c55199da, branch aix432-s3 @ 1f9df8efdf

reset.fixture: A logged-in CDE session on AIX 4.3.3 at 1024x768x8 (RS/6000 7020 40P under TCG), front panel and dtwm frames drawn by AIX's own GXT130P DDX through the emulated Matrox, with Netscape Communicator 4.08 on the retronet corpus web. Baked 2026-08-26 from a cold boot to a fresh dtlogin login -- NOT a resumed session, because a golden captured through a held pointer grab restores with clicks swallowed. Restore is proven through the production launcher: no firmware POST, no skipfix, clicks actuate.

museum.blurb: IBM's own Unix on IBM's own PowerPC workstation: AIX 4.3.3 booting to a full CDE desktop on an RS/6000, the machine that carried IBM's Unix business from the 1990s into the POWER era — and the desktop every other workstation vendor eventually standardised on.
museum.notes: Candidate, not on the floor. The real 7020-40P shipped a PowerPC 601; QEMU has no 601 model, so the exhibit runs a 604 — which is precisely why the genuine IBM boot ROM asserts 'time went negative' on its 601 clock path and needs PREP_TB_FREQ=15000000 plus a skipped POST settimeofday to boot at all. Graphics are a Matrox MGA device model written for this station and claimed by AIX as the GXT130P: the first natively graphical AIX under emulation we know of, against a Virtual OS Museum that reaches CDE only over XDMCP. It is AIX 4.3.3 and not the originally scoped 4.3.2 because 4.3.2's installer kernel stops driving the emulated LSI 53c810 after one retry cycle — measured, see docs/lab/research/candidate-aix.md.

emulator.source: github.com/Wnt/qemu @ aix432-s3 (11.0.2 + Poussineau's S3 Trio port + a new hw/display/mga.c + Tarasenko's lsi/raven AIX fixes + a PS/2 set-3 ACK fix), built to /opt/qemu-ppc-s3

network.note: retronet web plane only. The guest's NIC is bridged onto vmbr-rn through the persistent tap aixrn0 and addressed inside the guest with no default route, so it reaches the retronet gateway CT and nothing else, in either direction; the bridge has no uplink. Declared rather than derived because no launcher exists yet for the device ledger to be read from. docs/lab/retronet/STATION-aix432.md

notes: Tier 1 host-native station; slot 171 / UDP 54171 claimed via kh-claim, retronet 10.99.0.28 / tap aixrn0 claimed with it.

DISABLED CANDIDATE: not in the streamhost, signal, bring-up, golden, action-map or SPA lineups. Two things gate promotion — (1) a restore-proven golden baked against a TRACKED launcher, (2) streamhost/stations/aix432/ actually existing so runtime.qemu.launcher/envFixture/emitArgs can be filled. Slot 171 / UDP 54171 is INSIDE ports.publicRelayLow..High (54080-54200) in registry/registry-v1.json, so the relay port is no longer a gate — the station is still not promotable on the two reasons above.

Slot 171 was chosen after the walk-in clone pool's reservation was re-cut from 152-200 down to 152-170 (docs/lab/WALKIN-BRIEF.md) — the pool only ever used 152-160, and the station fleet had run out of relay-window slots, so the top of the reservation was given back. The scaffolder's allocator does not know about the walk-in reservation and would have handed out 152.

Known not to work, and not to be claimed anywhere visitor-facing: CorelDRAW 3.5 (needs an AIX 3.2-era libX11.a(shr.o) that 4.3 does not ship), Abuse's window (runs, stays black), and the MGA hardware cursor (unimplemented — the pointer is invisible).
